goal: Measure per-role effort and model choice on graded held-out cases with metered usage, and record the resulting curve in DESIGN-NOTES
asset: Feature-template role settings (architect, builder, red-team), the sweep.py split, and the effort record in DESIGN-NOTES
scope: Role-shaped graded cases for builder, red-team and architect with reference answers
A runner that calls authenticated headless Claude Code per (model, effort, case, rep) and records metered usage
A case-clustered paired comparison against each role's shipped setting, with the cheaper pick chosen on train only
A recorded sweep, its reading in DESIGN-NOTES, and the shipped role defaults the held-out results support
outOfScope: Whole-campaign sweeps through /fluxpoint:graph-run (council, judges, repair rounds and harness gates)
Changing the cost model's assumed multipliers in compile-graph.py
Choosing a model per role in shipped templates

record.question: How should #67 measure per-role effort and model choice with real usage?

options.strongest_objection: One role call in isolation can be easier than the same role inside a campaign, so a flat curve may not transfer
A binary harness score needs about 93 held-out runs per variant to see a 20-point difference, at tens of millions of tokens per variant

record.rationale: Graded scores per role resolve far smaller differences per run than a pass/fail campaign, the meter reports real cost per call, and the existing sweep.py split keeps the selection honest.
evidence: plugins/fluxpoint/DESIGN-NOTES.md, the sample-size arithmetic for a binary campaign score
Issue #67 asks for a per-role effort and model grid recorded in DESIGN-NOTES

costs.cost: About 700 metered headless calls for a 3 x 3 grid over 26 cases at 3 repetitions
evidence: Pilot runs reported total_cost_usd between 0.003 and 0.15 per call

costs.cost: About 32.6M estimated tokens for a four-variant plan that resolves only a 40-point difference
evidence: sweep.py --plan over the feature template, recorded in DESIGN-NOTES

requirements.statement: Every case's grader scores its reference answer 1.0 and a stub below 1.0, and seed or decoy markers never reach the fixture the model reads
requirements.counterexample: A red-team grader that scores a decoy finding as a hit, or a builder case whose hidden tests the reference fails

requirements.statement: The split is stratified by role and holds out cases of every role, and the cheaper pick is chosen from train-split differences only
requirements.counterexample: A pick that reads test-split scores, or a role with no held-out case

requirements.statement: Every graded run in the recorded sweep names the model that served it and carries the meter's cost, and the report excludes errored runs
requirements.counterexample: A recorded run served by a fallback model counted under the requested model, or an errored run graded as a zero

checks.scope: Every bench case's grader against its reference and a stub, grading rules, split, report, and the integrity of the recorded sweep file
assumptions: Graded role calls in isolation stand in for the same role inside a campaign only as far as DESIGN-NOTES states
The recorded results file is the output of run.py --run against an authenticated Claude Code; the check verifies its internal consistency, not that the calls happened

challenges.claim: Do isolated role calls show what a campaign needs?
challenges.resolution: No. They bound what one call of each role needs on cases of this size. DESIGN-NOTES states that limit beside the curve, and shipped defaults change only where the held-out cases support it.

challenges.claim: Were fixtures changed after seeing model output?
challenges.resolution: Yes, before the recorded sweep: pilot runs exposed unseeded real defects in some red-team fixtures and a ceiling in the builder cases. Fixtures were corrected and harder builder cases added before any recorded run; no fixture changed during or after it.
